name: Ab Testing Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building ab testing — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary ab testing tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building ab testing — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary ab testing tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple ab testing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Validate ab testing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Prefer explicit, readable ab testing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. Document any non-obvious ab testing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen ab testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Keep ab testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to ab testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop ab testing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated ab testing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of ab testing correctness.
- Avoid introducing new ab testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for ab testing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
